target_customer: Investors and traders wanting to hold and trade precious metals and other hard assets using bitcoin
problem: Serica, formerly DigitalTangible, ran a browser based wallet linking physical precious metals to the blockchain using Counterparty tokens, aiming to widen to other tangible assets.
business_model: Trading platform with fees on asset trades and custody

founders.name: Taariq Lewis
founders.background_notes: Named as founder and CEO by Cointelegraph. YC page lists no founder names.

exit.reason: CEO said compliance costs were too high for a startup, peer to peer hard asset trading was a smaller problem than hoped, and other more profitable business existed for the technology.

competitors.name: Vaultoro
competitors.what: Bitcoin to gold exchange, quoted in coverage of Serica's closure but not framed as a direct rival

technical_complexity.rationale: Building a wallet and trading front end on Counterparty tokens backed by custodied metals is moderate engineering, with the harder part being custody and compliance.

defensibility.rationale: The CEO said competitors had easier legal clearance and bigger compliance budgets, and tokens on an open protocol were easy to replicate.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent action found. The business closed itself in December 2015.

market_need_then: Coverage in April 2015 described customers wanting fast trades across tangible assets and bitcoin, but the CEO later said peer to peer hard asset trading was a smaller problem than hoped.

branding.name_origin: Lewis said the name comes from a Greek word associated with the people of the land where silk comes from, chosen when DigitalTangible rebranded to widen beyond precious metals.
branding.domain_note: Used sericapay.com, which no longer resolved.

rebrands.why: To expand beyond gold and precious metals into any valuable physical asset and digital money.

branding.community_and_virality: Crypto trade press covered the rebrand and the closure.

brand_strength.rationale: A brand change within a year of founding and a closure eight months later left little brand equity.

pivots.to: Other fintech opportunities such as healthcare payments
pivots.why: Compliance costs and a smaller than hoped peer to peer market.

outcome_analysis: Serica launched as DigitalTangible in September 2014, rebranded in April 2015, joined YC S15 and closed its hard asset trading business in December 2015. The CEO cited compliance costs that favored better funded rivals and a smaller peer to peer market than expected. A later database entry describes it as a healthcare payments company, consistent with the stated move into other fintech, and lists it as dead.
notes: The website sericapay.com did not resolve (DNS error). The 120K seed rests on a single database (CB Insights, via search summary). The YC page lists no founder names; Taariq Lewis comes from Cointelegraph. Vaultoro is not described as a rival by the source and the source is dated about four months after the batch. The Cointelegraph launch article names no competitors. Whether the later healthcare payments product shipped is unverified. Founder education and employers not found.
